text:
alice-cs: FYI escalation from AcmePayments. They say the JSON payload from our /v1/generate structured-output endpoint started returning strings for numeric fields and dropping the `transaction_id` key after last night's rollout. They pasted examples.

dan_acme: This started around 2026-03-14 22:10 UTC right after we swapped to redwood-llama-3b-v3 in canary. Before: 
```json
{
  "transaction_id": 1245789,
  "amount_cents": 2599,
  "currency": "USD",
  "items": [ { "sku": "X-100", "qty": 1 } ]
}
```
Now (from same prompt):
```json
{
  "transaction_id": "1245789",
  "amount_cents": "2599",
  "currency": "USD",
  "items": [ { "sku": "X-100", "qty": null } ]
}
```
We rely on types for downstream validation and the payment pipeline started rejecting these. Customer attached a couple of request IDs: r_3a8f2 and r_3a8f9.

alice-cs: They also say some requests completely omit `transaction_id` (null/absent) and sometimes items array comes back empty. Can we triage? They asked for rollback if this is from the rollout. :grimacing:

deploy-bot: canary rollout redwood-llama-3b-v3 -> prod complete @03:45 UTC, rollout id ro_20260314_2315 (success)

bob-oncall: I'm pulling traces and the two request IDs. Matching logs: r_3a8f2 shows model variant redwood-llama-3b-v3, prompt hashed, content-length on response looks normal but parser warnings in service: 
```
WARN schema-validator - path items[0].qty expected integer got null (request r_3a8f2)
WARN schema-transform - coerced number -> string for amount_cents (request r_3a8f9)
```
Also seeing a tiny spike in latency for that variant (p50 +12ms). Not sure if related.

carol-ml: This pattern (numbers as strings, null inside numeric slots) often shows up when the model emits quoted numbers or odd tokenization boundaries. Change in generation distribution from v2->v3 could cause that. Were there any tokenizer or postprocessing changes in v3?

dave-platform: V3 release only changed model weights and updated kernel selection for attention; no parser or postprocess changes. Rollout config used automatic structured-output extraction with our JSON-schema enforcement step turned on.

alice-cs: Customer says they had a pinned model before but we rolled forward to the new default at release time. They want either rollback or an immediate mitigation.

carol-ml: Quick repro steps for us: hit /v1/generate with same prompt and system instruction that enforces strict schema. Example prompt payload included in the customer attachment (sanitized):
```
{"model":"redwood-llama-3b-v3","input":"Fill the invoice JSON for the given transaction: <transaction data omitted>. Respond ONLY with valid JSON matching schema.","options":{"structured_output_schema":"/schemas/payment_v1.json","max_tokens":200}}
```
Repro harness I suggest: 1000 runs with seed variation and different temperature (0.0, 0.2, 0.5) to measure rate of schema violations. Also run against redwood-llama-3b-v2 for baseline.

bob-oncall: I'm running a quick 100 requests now against v3 and v2 with the customer's example. Early findings: v3 violations ~7/100, v2 violations 0/100 (for same prompts). The failures are mostly: numbers quoted, qty->null, missing transaction_id.

alice-cs: Customer is blocking production. They asked for an immediate rollback to v2 for their tenant only, or a global rollback if that is safer. They prefer tenant-scoped rollback if possible.

dave-platform: We can pin customer to redwood-llama-3b-v2 via tenant routing in ~10-15 mins. Global rollback for the model would be slower and affects other customers; recommend tenant pin for AcmePayments while we debug.

carol-ml: Plan: 1) Pin AcmePayments to v2 (dave) 2) Run prolonged repro harness + collect model outputs and token-level logits for violating cases (carol) 3) Add targeted prompt tweaks / schema priming to see if postprocessing can be tightened (bob/carol) 4) If issue persists and we find model weight cause, schedule revert of v3 global rollout.

bob-oncall: Actioning pin now and will post confirmation. Also creating a test suite PR to run these structured-output regression tests on every rollout.

bob-oncall: Pinned tenant acme_payments -> redwood-llama-3b-v2 (route id route_4521). Confirmed by routing logs showing 100% hits to v2 for that tenant.

alice-cs: Told customer we pinned them and to validate. They responded: "thanks, initial reports look better, but can you confirm we won't see this again? Our ingestion fails on any schema mismatch."

carol-ml: For long term: we should add schema-aware generation signals during compilation — i.e., prefer deterministic seeds for structured outputs and surface a "schema-confidence" score in the response. Also add stricter postprocess rules: reject if types mismatch instead of coercing. For now, I'll collect offending examples and run ablation on v3 to identify layer/attention changes correlating with the drift.

dave-platform: Filed infra ticket INF-2026-78 to add a pre-deployment structured-output canary that runs the customer's schema test corpus. We'll prioritize this.

alice-cs: Todo summary: @dave-platform pin tenant (done), @carol-ml run diagnostics & collect logits (in progress), @bob-oncall add regression test to rollout pipeline (in flight), @alice-cs follow up with customer and log RCA expectations. I'll update this thread with customer confirmation and final RCA. :white_check_mark:

dan_acme: Confirmed — ingestion resumed, no more rejects in first 200 transactions. Please keep me posted on the root cause and ETA for global fix.

bob-oncall: Note for engineers: reproduction harness snippet I'm adding to the ticket: 
```
for temp in [0.0,0.2,0.5]:
  for i in range(1000):
    call /v1/generate model=redwood-llama-3b-v3 prompt=<customer prompt> seed=i temp=temp options={structured_output_schema: payment_v1.json}
    validate output with ajv; log failures and token logits
```

carol-ml: If anyone needs the failing samples, I pushed them to the secure S3 bucket s3://redwood-debug/acme_regressions/v3/ (access for eng and sec only). I'll post initial triage by EOD.

alice-cs: Thanks everyone. Leaving this open until we have RCA. Closing note: customer happy with pin for now but wants a permanent assurance. We'll use the regression tests in release gating moving forward.
